summary: The published day-five bars reproduce the Data 11 adjusted-P rule (319 up, 68 down), while the notebook reproduces its nominal-P rule (360 up, 92 down). The deposited analysis uses nine FGF1 and fourteen vehicle mice, and only the authors can reconcile the seven vehicle mice labelled Non-Diabetic with the manuscript’s eligibility criterion and reported sample size.

manualReview.summary: Published day-five DEG counts are reconciled. Eligibility of seven vehicle mice needs author confirmation.
manualReview.note: Figure 7a and Data 11 agree at adjusted P < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 0.5. The notebook uses nominal P for its own plot. The count matrix, per-GSM characteristics, deposited group assignments and registered samplesheet identify the same nine FGF1 and fourteen vehicle libraries at day five. The authors’ six-group DESeq2 model includes all 47 libraries. A check of its normalized means from deposited counts supports this membership, including the Gbp2 outlier replacement. The day-five-only edgeR-QL fit is the registered result. Its current DE table contains 4,980 FDR calls, including 1,763 shared with Data 11 and five outside that workbook’s day-five sheet. Evidence and replay are in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE153551/codex-2026-11-21/SEARCH_LOG.md and results.json.
reviewFlags: Figure 7a and the bulk Methods give seven vehicle mice. GEO labels seven of the fourteen day-five controls Non-Diabetic. The public materials lack animal-linked pretreatment glucose and an eligibility decision for those controls.
The two fits share a day-five treatment contrast and differ in normalization, dispersion fitting and inference. Missing author rows have unassessed author P and FDR.

evidenceLinks.label: Published study, Figure 7a and bulk RNA-seq Methods

verificationReview.reason: Data 11 and the current registered table were compared across all 14,193 published day-five genes. Published Figure 7a follows the adjusted-P rule, and the author notebook’s nominal-P plot accounts for the alternate counts. The deposit and code establish which libraries entered the fit. Animal-level baseline eligibility remains unresolved because the manuscript specifies diabetic mice and seven controls, while the analysis includes fourteen day-five controls, seven labelled Non-Diabetic.
verificationReview.nextStep: Which day-five vehicle mice met the pretreatment diabetes criterion, when was the GEO diabetes label assigned, and which control GSMs did the authors intend Figure 7a and Data 11 to represent? Retain the standardized day-five-only edgeR-QL result for Explorer and describe the joint-timepoint DESeq2 result as the author reference. Revisit the cohort interpretation when an animal-to-library eligibility key or a correction becomes available.

comparabilityReview.basis: Current registered day-five-only bulk edgeR-QL FGF1-minus-vehicle table, SHA-256 1e1c274bc4cb6f817b5f0657f4860ff8c28c38368a202aef1fcffd086b2ec00e.
comparabilityReview.reference: Supplementary Data 11, sheet b.d5_deg. Published Figure 7a, author notebook, GSE153549 bulk counts, metadata and GSM records support interpretation. See data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE153551/codex-2026-11-21/SOURCES.tsv.

cohort.note: The deposited day-five membership matches Explorer by sample ID and arm. Each GSM represents one mouse. Both include 9 FGF1 and 14 vehicle mice. Eligibility for the manuscript’s diabetic cohort is unresolved for the seven controls labelled Non-Diabetic. The caption and bulk Methods report 9 versus 7.

contrast.note: Both coefficients estimate day-five FGF1 minus pair-fed vehicle in bulk ob/ob mouse hypothalamus. The author coefficient is a day-specific contrast in a six-group model fitted across time points.

features.note: All 14,193 published day-five gene symbols join uniquely to the registered IDs. Of 28 additional registered genes, 25 fail the author count filter. F5, Parpbp and Sostdc1 pass it. Each has a Cook’s-distance lower bound above the author software’s cutoff in a group with fewer than seven mice, corroborating the earlier Cook-filtering attribution.

effects.note: Both estimates are log2 treatment-to-vehicle effects. On 14,193 finite nonzero pairs Pearson is 0.99525826, Spearman is 0.99539372, and 13,499 signs agree (95.1103%). The median absolute log2FC difference is 0.0141811. The Gbp2 replacement in the author model accounts for a specific sign reversal.

inference.note: Published DESeq2 uses all 47 libraries in six groups. Registered edgeR-QL uses the 23 day-five libraries. At FDR < 0.05 the author calls 1,766 and Explorer calls 4,975 on paired tests, sharing 1,763. Five further Explorer calls lack author inference. Recalculation identifies BH adjustment in Data 11. Figure 7a uses the caption’s FDR and effect cutoffs.

coverage.note: The full day-five author sheet is present. Finite effects and adjusted P values pair for 14,193/14,193 reference rows and 14,193/14,221 registered rows (99.8031% output coverage). The remaining 28 genes lack author rows.

comparabilityReview.criteria: Use the prespecified day-five sheet, exact unique IDs, original coefficient direction and all finite effect pairs. Apply author-concordance-v2 sample-size, coverage and alternative correlation/direction criteria. Compare whole-list and paired-test FDR < 0.05 calls separately. Evaluate each documented Figure 7a threshold with the same strict |log2FC| > 0.5 cutoff.
comparabilityReview.conclusion: Both numerical v2 routes and the coverage criterion are met for the deposited results. The biological eligibility question limits cohort compatibility. Retain the registered day-five analysis and keep the author all-timepoint fit as a separate reference. Full sign-off remains open.
